plain: The recommended way to put an error bar on a share like 48 out of 60; it stays sensible with few items or extreme rates.
eli5: A smarter “give or take” for small counts, which never says less than none or more than all.
technical: Wilson (1927) score interval: invert the score test for a binomial proportion. Unlike the Wald interval p̂ ± z√(p̂(1−p̂)/n), its centre is pulled toward ½ and it stays inside [0, 1]; Brown, Cai and DasGupta (2001) recommend it for small n.
